archetypes.name: path-grant-audit
archetypes.rationale: The security property rests on the claim that dirname "$round_dir" falls outside Codex's --add-dir and --full-auto write grants; if the dispatch invocation grants the parent dir, relocation is hollow.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read the Codex dispatch call sites in review-and-fix.sh around line 273 and any callers in review-implement-step5-loop.sh. Identify every --add-dir, --workspace, and -C flag passed to codex exec and map the exact filesystem roots they grant. Verify that the proposed snapshot sibling path (dirname "$round_dir"/.pre-coder-snapshots/...) falls outside all granted roots, not merely outside $round_dir itself. Check whether $IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR is always set to an absolute path that is not a subdirectory of $PWD or any --add-dir root. Confirm that the plan's Cursor-path note (--workspace "$PWD", never reaches round_dir) matches the actual dispatch invocation for Cursor rounds in the same scripts. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: reader-writer-sweep
archetypes.rationale: The plan's own failure-mode #1 warns that any missed pre-coder-* reader or writer left at the old round_dir path silently mis-resolves; the plan enumerates some sites but a single missed literal would break the security guarantee.
archetypes.prompt_body: Scan review-and-fix.sh and review-implement-step5-loop.sh for every literal string occurrence of pre-coder-head.txt, pre-coder-tracked-paths.txt, and pre-coder-path-diffs (both as path components and as variable substrings). For each occurrence, determine whether it is a pre-dispatch write (must move to snapshot dir), a post-dispatch write (must stay in round_dir), or a read (must be repointed to match its corresponding write). Cross-check the plan's enumerated sites against this full occurrence list and flag any occurrence the plan does not account for. Also check test-review-and-fix.sh for stale $round_dir/pre-coder-path-diffs/... literals that the plan's negative-control rm -f update is meant to replace, and verify the worktree negative-control path resolves through pre_coder_path_diff_file rather than a hardcoded string. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: mav-head-only-parity
archetypes.rationale: The plan intentionally relocates only pre-coder-head.txt on MAV rounds and explicitly forbids calling snapshot_pre_coder_tracked_state there; if MAV currently writes or reads tracked-paths or path-diffs, the plan silently leaves those at the old location.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read the run_implement_mav_apply function in review-implement-step5-loop.sh and trace every pre-coder-* file it currently writes or reads (head, tracked-paths, path-diffs). Verify that today MAV writes only pre-coder-head.txt and reads no tracked-paths or path-diffs files in its own scope, confirming the plan's head-only parity claim. If MAV reads any carryover predicate that internally reads pre-coder-tracked-paths.txt or path-diff patches, confirm the plan's note that those predicates fail closed when the snapshot is absent rather than silently returning stale data from round_dir. Check whether the location-invariant assertion proposed for test-review-and-fix.sh tests both the main-round and MAV-round snapshot paths or only main rounds; a MAV-round path with a different dirname structure would escape the invariant. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
